name: Republic of Finland

areaKm2.note: League of Nations Year-Book 1939/40: 388,279 km2 incl. inland water (high); world_1938 Finland polygon = ~368,000 km2 computed on the sphere (low).

population.note: League of Nations Year-Book 1939/40: Finland 3.63M (31 Dec 1937, low); COW NMC v7 tpop 1939 = 3,700k (high).

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share Finland 1940 = 30.8% (high); Finnish statistics counted ~27% in towns and boroughs in 1939 (mid 0.25). Low = COW upop/tpop 1939 = 304/3,700 = 0.08 (cities over 100,000).

activePersonnel.note: Cited page: at the beginning of the war the Finns had 300,000 soldiers; maximum strength 346,000 in uniform in March 1940 (Palokangas, via the cited page). Snapshot date: 30 November 1939. Check: COW NMC v7 milper 1939 = 37k (annual averages, not the snapshot-date strength).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Older reservists and Civic Guard (Suojeluskunta) members not yet called; the YH refresher mobilisation of October 1939 had already called most trained men.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Trotter, A Frozen Hell (isbn:1-56512-249-6), not read from a fetched source. Artillery, engineers, signals, supply (horse-drawn), coast artillery, navy (~5,000), air force (~2,500) (Trotter, A Frozen Hell ch. 3).

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Low read from the Winter War page; mid recalled from the Continuation War peak, not read from a fetched source. Winter War peak 346,000 (cited page) / 3.69M = 0.094 (low); the Continuation War peak of ~530,000 (14%) shows the deeper potential (mid;).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Trotter, A Frozen Hell (isbn:1-56512-249-6), not read from a fetched source. 9 infantry divisions (~14,000 men, ~9,000-10,000 riflemen each) on mobilisation plus separate battalions on the Karelian Isthmus and Ladoga front.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: M/28-30 rifles, Suomi KP/-31 SMG and Lahti-Saloranta LMG; cited page: 250,028 rifles for 300,000 men; almost no AT guns

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: reservists, YH refresher training Oct-Nov 1939, ski-trained

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Trotter, A Frozen Hell (isbn:1-56512-249-6), not read from a fetched source. Separate battalions, ski and guerrilla (sissi) units in Lapland and the wilderness (Suomussalmi, Kuhmo).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: SMGs and skis

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: expert winter fighters

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Trotter, A Frozen Hell (isbn:1-56512-249-6), not read from a fetched source. Cavalry Brigade (2 regiments).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: mounted infantry

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: regulars and reservists

count.note: Cited page: 32 Renault FT (used as pillboxes) and 32 Vickers 6-ton delivered without weapons; only 10 fit for combat at the start (low).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: 1918 tanks and unarmed Vickers

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25. Evidence: the one tank attack (Honkaniemi, Feb 1940) failed

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Trotter, A Frozen Hell (isbn:1-56512-249-6), not read from a fetched source. ~400-500 field guns and howitzers of mixed 1900-1920s types (Trotter ch. 3), plus coast artillery (excluded).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: old Russian guns, chronic shell shortage

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: accurate fire control

count.note: Cited page: 114 combat aeroplanes fit for duty on 1 December 1939; ~46 of them fighters (Fokker D.XXI and Bristol Bulldog).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Fokker D.XXI fixed-undercarriage fighter

training.note: Rubric row: training 1.0 (elite). Evidence: Finnish Air Force page: Finnish fighters credited with 218 Soviet aircraft for 47 lost in air combat

count.note: Cited page: 114 combat aeroplanes minus fighters = ~68 Bristol Blenheim bombers and Fokker C.X / C.V reconnaissance aircraft.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: 17 Blenheims, rest biplanes

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional crews

count.note: Coastal defence ships Vainamoinen and Ilmarinen.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: small coast defence ships with 254 mm guns

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: AA defence of Turku

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1922-1946 (isbn:0-85177-146-7), not read from a fetched source. 4 gunboats (Turunmaa, Karjala, Uusimaa, Hameenmaa), minelayers and motor torpedo boats (Conway's 1922-1946).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: small craft

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: archipelago operations

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1922-1946 (isbn:0-85177-146-7), not read from a fetched source. Vetehinen, Vesihiisi, Iku-Turso, Saukko, Vesikko (Conway's).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: German-designed small boats

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: little action in the ice

count.note: Educated guess. AA batteries: Bofors 40 mm and 76 mm guns defending Helsinki, Turku and Viipuri.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Bofors guns

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: effective against unescorted bombers

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75. Evidence: Mannerheim and his staff; motti tactics at Suomussalmi and Raate road; Mannerheim Line held two months

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75-1.0. Evidence: homogeneous army, local recruitment, 1918 divisions healed by 1939

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 1.0 (fanatical). Evidence: the spirit of the Winter War: national survival

weapons.note: Anchor: between 7 (1905) and 8 (1943). Evidence: Suomi SMG, Lahti-Saloranta LMG, Bofors 37 mm AT gun (few); improvised Molotov cocktails

armor.note: Anchor: 7 (armoured cars, helmets). Evidence: virtually no tanks

ships.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: coast defence ships and small submarines

fortification.note: Anchor: between 7 (concrete forts) and 8. Evidence: Mannerheim Line: ~100 concrete bunkers plus field works, tank obstacles; coast artillery forts

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (railways). Evidence: rail to the Isthmus, horses and skis; road-bound Soviet columns were cut by mottis

communications.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: telephone networks; radio intelligence broke Soviet codes

isr.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: radio intelligence and ski patrols

air.note: Anchor: between 7 (1914) and 8 (1943). Evidence: Fokker D.XXI, Bristol Blenheim; Brewster and Fiat G.50 arrived Feb 1940

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Defence ~3% of GDP in 1938 (low); the YH mobilisation from October and war spending in 1940 approached ~45% (high).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Forest industries, metal and textiles ~28% of output; ~55% of the labour force in agriculture.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment. Herrendorf et al. via OWID: Finland agriculture share of employment 1930 = 69.8%, 1940 = 61.9%; interpolation to 1939 = ~62.7%. 1 - 0.627 = 0.37 (mid). Near self-sufficient; grain imports needed in the war years.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Men reaching 21 per year (births ~80,000 c. 1918, half male, ~85% survival).

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. Fokker D.XXI licence-built by the State Aircraft Factory (Valtion lentokonetehdas), ~38 from 1937-39 and 50 more in 1940-41.

artillery.note: Educated guess. Field guns and mortars per year from Tampella and state works.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Public roads, mostly gravel.

railKm.note: CHAT railline Finland: 1938 = 5,740 km, 1939 = 5,864 km (1940 = 4,596 km after the Moscow Peace cessions).

majorPorts.note: Helsinki, Turku, Kotka, Viipuri, Vaasa, Oulu; Petsamo (Arctic).

merchantTonnage.note: League of Nations Year-Book 1939/40 table: Finnish merchant fleet 580,000 GRT (June 1938). Converted to deadweight at x1.5 (low x1.3 of the low GRT, high x1.6 of the high GRT).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Horse-drawn and ski supply in roadless forest; fighting close to own railways.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. ~380,000 horses in Finland in 1939; ~74,000 requisitioned.

chokepoints: Raate road and the waist of Finland (Suomussalmi)

homeDefense.note: 1.3 row: forests, lakes, winter and motivated population; the Soviet road-bound columns were destroyed in the wilderness.

notes: Snapshot date 30 November 1939 (Soviet invasion). YH (extra refresher training) mobilisation from 14 October 1939. Forces are the whole Finnish army; ~130,000 men on the Karelian Isthmus. Aircraft from the Winter War infobox (114 fit for combat, 173 total plus 43 reserve). Ship convention per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries: battleships, carriers, cruisers and destroyers = ships_major, torpedo boats and smaller craft = ships_minor (role split per SOURCES.md naval role boundaries).
